assertions: The default policy is shared.
Messages from different senders reuse the same runtime session.
The reused session can be closed canonically.
Concurrent senders get distinct sessions and both dispatch before either completes.
A follow-up reuses its sender's session and preserves ordering.
Reversed completion order preserves exact parent message, body and recipient attribution.
A fresh DB connection resolves durable sender affinity; after close a new session is opened.
Changing policy while sessions are active is refused.
Two verified source sessions of the same actor separate only in per_sender_session mode.
Separate source sessions dispatch concurrently in that mode; per_sender serializes them.
A verified source-session follow-up reuses its prior runtime session.
Sessionless traffic has its own scope only in per_sender_session; unverified attribution cannot create a privileged scope.
Published runtime-origin references and foreign keys remain coherent.
The second call queues while the first runs.
The first call succeeds and its session is CLOSED before the next call uses a distinct session.
All one-shot slots are released after completion.
The first call claims the prepared warm session exactly.
That session closes and is not reused for the next call.
Handoffs share the one-shot capacity and queue.
Each handoff retains its exact canonical claim and a distinct session.
The real Connector WebSocket path queues two calls, receives canonical results and stops each synthetic native peer.
The two calls open exactly two distinct sessions; both session and lease states become CLOSED.

rows.mode: new R3 receipt seam, without an invented cross-product requirement
assertions: A client_request_id creates one canonical delivery, one open/turn pair and one execution charge.
Three identical retries reuse the same receipt and do not change the snapshot or create a second native open/send.

scope_limits: Native peers, provider candidates and identities are synthetic. Adapter labels do not qualify installed provider binaries or paid turns.
SQLite, application transactions, canonical MCP/HTTP paths, the installed Core contract and the selected remote Connector WebSocket path are real.
Shared/per_sender/per_sender_session coverage is embedded; only the selected one_shot case exercises remote Connector transport.
This does not claim a client_request_id-by-four-modes Cartesian matrix; RG-04 does not explicitly require that new target.
No personal vault, native Windows service, user credentials, reboot/logon or real-client M1/M2 campaign is exercised.
No checkout, ledger, plan or historical artifact change is authorized or performed by this campaign.
